sections.html: Corydoras orphnopterus was described in 1970 on the basis of three specimens collected by an unknown collector at an undocumented time in Ecuador, in the lower Rio Bobonaza between Montalvo (2°06’S, 76°59’W) and Chicherota (2°22’S, 76°38’W), province of Pastaza. The Rio Bobonaza belongs to the catchment area of the Rio Pastaza, which in turn flows into the Amazon in Peru.

This long-nosed Corydoras catfish has the following unique combination of colour characteristics: a dark eye mask; a black spot in the dorsal fin, most intense at the front edge of the centre of the fin; a pattern of relatively small dots forming three parallel lines on the caudal peduncle in the middle of the body, between which the whitish basic colour of the body is lighter than on the rest of the body, resulting in two light bands; and a pattern of approximately 6–7 thin bands in the caudal fin, which are dissolved into individual spots.

Because the collecting location of the fish from Peru was initially unknown, because details of the colour pattern were coarser than in the holotype of C. orphnopterus, and because nothing is known about the colour variance of C. orphnopterus, these animals were called CW58 in the hobby as a precaution.

The imported fish show the large individual range of colour patterns typical for long-nosed corys, and each individual can be recognised by its pattern. Some correspond almost in every detail to the holotype of C. orphnopterus, others are roughly patterned fish of type CW58, with all conceivable transitions in between. From the similar, also highly variable Corydoras leopardus, C. orphnopterus and CW58 are always distinguished by the dark eye band, which is missing in C. leopardus.

Taking all the facts together, CW58 is, according to current knowledge, a variant of Corydoras orphnopterus originating from the Rio Tigre. Some doubts remain, because no living specimens from the Rio Bobonaza are known yet.
